summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of systolic heart failure (EF 30%), atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and obesity was admitted for chest discomfort and shortness of breath. The chest pain was burning, non-exertional, and resolved with club soda, with stable troponins and no EKG changes, ruling out acute coronary syndrome. The symptoms were attributed to GERD or musculoskeletal causes, possibly triggered by alcohol. He had acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation due to fluid overload, likely from dietary indiscretion and medication noncompliance. He was treated with IV Lasix, then transitioned to oral torsemide, resulting in an 18-pound weight loss and symptom improvement. During admission, he developed right foot cellulitis with a fluid collection, which was drained at bedside twice; wound culture grew MSSA, and he completed a course of vancomycin with a planned two-week course of oral dicloxacillin. Due to chronically unstable INR and a CHADS score of 5, he was transitioned from warfarin to Pradaxa. His insulin dose was reduced due to hypoglycemia, and plans were made to consider switching to glargine. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for podiatry, primary care, and colonoscopy for reported maroon stools.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
